concept.name: Airflow DAG Orchestration

relationships.description: Connects Airflow DAG Orchestration to data warehousing lakehouse in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Apache Airflow orchestrates batch data workflows as Python-defined Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), decoupling scheduling (`data_interval_start`) from compute execution across workers (CeleryExecutor or KubernetesExecutor) with built-in retries, backfills, and lineage.
spark.keyTakeaway: Airflow is a control plane, not a data-processing engine: keep DAG files lightweight, push heavy compute to Spark/dbt/Snowflake, and make every task idempotent over its `data_interval_start`.

concept.whyItMatters: Chaining brittle cron jobs breaks down as soon as an upstream S3 drop arrives 2 hours late, a downstream table needs a 90-day backfill, or two teams share dependencies. Airflow's scheduler, metadata database, and `data_interval` model give data teams deterministic retries, dependency graphs, SLA alerting, and one-command historical backfills.
whenToUse: Scheduled batch ELT/ETL pipelines (hourly, daily, weekly) coordinating S3/GCS, dbt, Spark, Snowflake, or BigQuery.
Complex dependency graphs with branching, sensor/deferrable waits for upstream files, and automated SLA alerts.
Historical backfills where each past date partition (`ds`) must be re-run deterministically.
whenNotToUse: Sub-second or continuous event streaming (use Apache Flink, Kafka Streams, or Spark Structured Streaming).
High-frequency (<1 minute) micro-jobs—Airflow's scheduler loop and task-startup overhead add seconds of latency per task.
Running multi-gigabyte Pandas transformations directly inside Airflow worker memory instead of delegating to external compute.
keyPoints: A DAG run represents a logical data interval (`data_interval_start` to `data_interval_end`), and the scheduler triggers the run *after* the interval closes.
Idempotency is non-negotiable: tasks must safely re-run on retry or backfill using partition overwrites (`INSERT OVERWRITE` / `MERGE`), never blind `APPEND`.
Airflow's Scheduler parses DAG Python files every ~30 seconds (`min_file_process_interval`), so top-level code must never make DB or HTTP calls.
Deferrable operators + the Triggerer process suspend long-running waits (`S3KeySensor`, `SnowflakeOperator`) in async `asyncio` loops instead of holding worker slots.
XCom (`xcom_push`/`xcom_pull`) stores small metadata (row counts, S3 URIs) in the metadata DB—never pass raw DataFrames or multi-MB payloads through it.

examples.title: Daily Orders Mart ELT with Partitioned Backfill
examples.scenario: An e-commerce data team needs `orders_daily` refreshed by 06:00 UTC using yesterday's Stripe and Postgres CDC drops in S3.
examples.outcome: A daily DAG waits via a deferrable `S3KeySensor`, triggers a Snowflake `COPY INTO` + `MERGE` keyed on `data_interval_start` (`ds`), runs `dbt test`, and posts to Slack on SLA miss—allowing a 30-day backfill with `airflow dags backfill` without duplicating rows.

examples.title: Dynamic Task Mapping Across 400 Regional Shards
examples.scenario: A retail pipeline must ingest daily POS files from a variable list of active store regions discovered at runtime.
examples.outcome: An upstream task lists active regions to XCom, and `ingest_region.expand(region=...)` dynamically spawns parallel mapped task instances in `KubernetesExecutor` pods without hard-coding 400 static tasks.

tradeOffs.pro: `CeleryExecutor` keeps warm worker processes running for low-latency (~1s) task startup on high-frequency DAGs.
tradeOffs.con: `KubernetesExecutor` isolates every task in its own pod with custom Docker images/resources, but adds 5–15s pod scheduling overhead.

tradeOffs.pro: Deferrable operators free the worker slot completely while waiting in the Triggerer's `asyncio` loop, cutting worker costs dramatically.
tradeOffs.con: Requires running the `Triggerer` component and writing/using async-compatible triggers.

tradeOffs.pro: Airflow Datasets (`outlets=[Dataset('s3://...')]`) decouple producer and consumer DAGs without fragile time-delta matching.
tradeOffs.con: Makes end-to-end lineage harder to visualize in a single DAG graph compared to unified task groups.

failureModes.name: Non-Idempotent Backfill Duplication
failureModes.description: A task uses `INSERT INTO target SELECT ...` without deleting or merging the target `ds` partition; retrying a failed run doubles revenue numbers.
failureModes.mitigation: Delete-and-insert by `ds`, use `MERGE`, or write to an immutable partition path (`s3://bucket/dt={{ ds }}/`) with atomic swap.

failureModes.name: Top-Level DAG Parsing Timeouts
failureModes.description: A developer puts `requests.get(...)` or `Variable.get(...)` at module import level; the Scheduler runs it every 30s across all DAGs, exhausting DB connections and timing out.
failureModes.mitigation: Move all I/O, SQL queries, and `Variable.get` calls inside task callables or Jinja templates (`{{ var.value.my_key }}`).

failureModes.name: XCom Metadata DB Bloat & Worker OOM
failureModes.description: Tasks pass 50 MB Pandas DataFrames via XCom, bloating Postgres `xcom` tables and crashing workers on `xcom_pull`.
failureModes.mitigation: Write intermediate datasets to S3/GCS/Snowflake and pass only the URI or table name via XCom.

failureModes.name: Zombie Tasks & Connection Pool Exhaustion
failureModes.description: Long-running Python tasks get OOM-killed without heartbeating, or 200 parallel tasks overwhelm a 20-connection Postgres warehouse.
failureModes.mitigation: Assign Airflow `Pools` (e.g., `postgres_pool` with 10 slots) to throttle concurrency against shared external databases.

commonMistakes: Using `datetime.now()` inside a task instead of `{{ ds }}` / `data_interval_start`, breaking historical backfills.
Setting `start_date=datetime.now()` in a DAG definition, which causes the scheduler's start boundary to shift on every parse.
Running heavy Spark/ML/Pandas compute inside the Airflow Scheduler or Worker instead of submitting jobs to EMR, Databricks, or K8s pods.
Leaving `catchup=True` unintentionally on a DAG with an old `start_date`, triggering thousands of unwanted historical runs on deploy.
Using `depends_on_past=True` without understanding that a single failed day stalls every subsequent day indefinitely.

sections.content:
## The idea

**Apache Airflow** treats data pipelines as **Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs)** authored in Python, where nodes are tasks (Operators/Sensors) and edges are execution dependencies. Rather than running scripts blindly on wall-clock cron, Airflow tracks every run against a **data interval** (`data_interval_start` to `data_interval_end`) persisted in a central **Metadata Database** (PostgreSQL).

Crucially, Airflow separates the **control plane** (Scheduler + Triggerer + Webserver) from the **execution plane** (Celery/Kubernetes workers) and the **compute plane** (Snowflake, BigQuery, Spark, dbt). Airflow orchestrates *when* and *in what order* work runs, while external engines do the heavy lifting.

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace a daily `revenue_mart` DAG scheduled at `@daily` (`0 0 * * *`) for `2026-11-11`:

1. **Interval Close & Scheduling**: At `2026-11-12 00:00 UTC`, the `2026-11-11` interval closes. The Scheduler reads the DAG's serialized definition from the Metadata DB and creates a `DagRun` with `ds = '2026-11-11'`.
2. **Deferrable Wait**: Task `wait_for_s3` (`S3KeySensor(deferrable=True)`) checks `s3://raw-events/dt=2026-11-11/_SUCCESS`. Not found yet—so it defers to the **Triggerer**, freeing its worker slot.
3. **Trigger & Resume**: At `00:14 UTC`, the Triggerer detects `_SUCCESS`, marks the trigger complete, and queues the downstream `load_snowflake` task.
4. **Idempotent Compute**: `KubernetesExecutor` launches a worker pod that executes `MERGE INTO orders_mart USING stage_2026_11_11 ...` against Snowflake.
5. **Verification & Lineage**: `dbt_test` validates `not_null` and `unique` on `order_id`. If any test fails, Airflow retries per `retries=2, retry_delay=5m` and fires an `on_failure_callback` to PagerDuty/Slack.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Execution model, deferrable operators & XCom limits
sections.content:
## Execution model, deferrable operators & XCom limits

Two architectural rules govern healthy Airflow deployments:

- **Never Poll on a Worker Slot**: Classic `poke`-mode sensors hold an entire worker process/pod idle while checking S3 or an API every 60 seconds. Switching to `deferrable=True` moves the wait into the **Triggerer**, where a single Python `asyncio` process can monitor thousands of concurrent waits using minimal RAM.
- **Keep XCom Small**: XCom is backed by a `BYTEA`/JSON column in PostgreSQL. Passing a 10 KB config dict or an S3 URI (`s3://bucket/run_123/part.parquet`) is ideal; passing a DataFrame triggers serialization bottlenecks and database bloat. Use an **Object Storage XCom Backend** if larger metadata exchange is unavoidable.

## Airflow executors compared

| Executor | Isolation Model | Task Startup Latency | Scaling & Ops | Best-Fit Workload |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **LocalExecutor** | Subprocesses on 1 host | < 1s | Single machine only | Dev environments, small teams (< 50 DAGs) |
| **CeleryExecutor** | Shared worker pools via Redis/RabbitMQ | ~1–2s | Autoscaling workers; shared Python env | High-frequency, uniform lightweight tasks |
| **KubernetesExecutor** | 1 Pod per TaskInstance | ~5–15s (pod spin-up) | Native K8s HPA; per-task Docker image/CPU/RAM | Heterogeneous workloads, strict dependency isolation |

## Failure modes

1. **Scheduler Parse Bottlenecks**: Heavy imports (`pandas`, `torch`) or API calls at the top level of DAG files stall the `DagFileProcessor`, delaying task scheduling across the entire cluster. *Fix*: Lazy-import heavy libraries inside `@task` functions.
2. **Non-Idempotent Retries**: Appending rows without partition keys corrupts tables on retry. *Fix*: Parameterize every write with `{{ ds }}` and use atomic `MERGE` or partition overwrite.
3. **Metadata DB Connection Exhaustion**: Scaling workers without PgBouncer saturates Postgres `max_connections`. *Fix*: Place PgBouncer in front of the Metadata DB and use Airflow `Pools` for external DBs.
4. **Unbounded Backfills**: Triggering a 2-year backfill with `max_active_runs=16` hammers downstream warehouses simultaneously. *Fix*: Set `max_active_runs=1` or `2` on heavy DAGs.

sections.eyebrow: 06 / DAG parsing hygiene, pools & SLA monitoring
sections.content:
## DAG parsing hygiene, pools & SLA monitoring

Enforce CI checks on every DAG PR: run `pytest` to verify `DagBag()` imports in under 2 seconds with zero import errors, and validate that no top-level code touches network sockets.

Use **Airflow Pools** (`--pool warehouse_writes --slots 8`) to protect downstream OLTP/OLAP databases from thundering herds during morning peaks, and configure `sla` / `execution_timeout` plus `on_failure_callback` alerts routed to PagerDuty or Slack.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Use static `start_date` values and `catchup=False` unless historical catchup is explicitly desired.
- [ ] Parameterize all reads/writes with `data_interval_start` / `{{ ds }}`—never `datetime.now()`.
- [ ] Keep top-level DAG files pure (no DB queries, HTTP calls, or `Variable.get()` outside tasks).
- [ ] Enable `deferrable=True` on all Sensors and long-running external job operators.
- [ ] Pass only S3/GCS URIs or small metadata via XCom—never raw datasets.
- [ ] Cap `max_active_runs` and configure `Pools` + `execution_timeout` on every production DAG.

interviewProblems.title: Airflow DAG Orchestration
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Airflow DAG Orchestration. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Apache Airflow orchestrates batch data workflows as Python-defined Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), decoupling scheduling (`data_interval_start`) from compute execution across workers (CeleryExecutor or KubernetesExecutor) with built-in retries, backfills, and lineage.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Executor & Workers applies the primary invariant and coordinates with External Compute.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, External Compute experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Delete-and-insert by `ds`, use `MERGE`, or write to an immutable partition path (`s3://bucket/dt={{ ds }}/`) with atomic swap.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Airflow is a control plane, not a data-processing engine: keep DAG files lightweight, push heavy compute to Spark/dbt/Snowflake, and make every task idempotent over its `data_interval_start`.
Avoid trap: Using `datetime.now()` inside a task instead of `{{ ds }}` / `data_interval_start`, breaking historical backfills.
Avoid trap: Setting `start_date=datetime.now()` in a DAG definition, which causes the scheduler's start boundary to shift on every parse.
When to reach for it: Scheduled batch ELT/ETL pipelines (hourly, daily, weekly) coordinating S3/GCS, dbt, Spark, Snowflake, or BigQuery.
When to reach for it: Complex dependency graphs with branching, sensor/deferrable waits for upstream files, and automated SLA alerts.

putItTogether.title: Putting Airflow Dag Orchestration Together
putItTogether.summary: Airflow is a control plane, not a data-processing engine: keep DAG files lightweight, push heavy compute to Spark/dbt/Snowflake, and make every task idempotent over its `data_interval_start`.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Airflow Dag Orchestration before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: A daily DAG waits via a deferrable `S3KeySensor`, triggers a Snowflake `COPY INTO` + `MERGE` keyed on `data_interval_start` (`ds`), runs `dbt test`, and posts to Slack on SLA miss—allowing a 30-day backfill with `airflow dags backfill` without duplicating rows.
